query: How does resolution time vary across issue themes, channel, and priority?

per_column.name: issue_theme
per_column.rationale: Themes are the core grouping axis the query asks for, giving strong new leverage. However several sample categorisations are wrong: CS-0004 (report pinning enhancement) labelled 'billing' and CS-0005 (CSV export BOM after release) labelled 'performance' contradict the text, indicating unreliable extraction.

per_column.name: theme_avg_resolution_minutes
per_column.rationale: A per-theme average is useful for comparison but is a derived aggregate largely redundant with grouping by issue_theme on resolution_minutes. Its correctness inherits the mislabelling of issue_theme, so grounding is only moderate.

per_column.name: channel_avg_resolution_minutes
per_column.rationale: Channel-level average supports the channel dimension of the query, but it is a straightforward group aggregate redundant with grouping on the existing channel column. Values are computable from the table.

per_column.name: priority_avg_resolution_minutes
per_column.rationale: Supports the priority dimension but is a redundant group aggregate over the existing priority column and resolution_minutes.

per_column.name: resolution_vs_theme_avg
per_column.rationale: A per-row deviation from the theme average is a genuinely useful modelling/comparison feature (outlier detection). Values are arithmetically derivable but depend on the flawed issue_theme assignment, lowering grounding.

per_column.name: priority_numeric
per_column.rationale: An ordinal encoding of priority enables modelling/sorting, a modest but real gain. However the mapping is inconsistent/ambiguous: CS-0002 and CS-0005 both map to 2 while priority ordering vs original label is unclear, and encodings appear not to align cleanly with a defensible severity order.

judge.rationale: The columns collectively target all three axes the query names (theme, channel, priority) and add a useful per-row deviation feature, so usefulness is solid, though the three group-average columns are partly redundant with simple group-bys on existing/added columns. Groundedness is the weaker dimension: issue_theme shows clear mislabelling in the samples (enhancement->billing, CSV/BOM->performance), and every derived column (theme averages, deviation) inherits that error, while priority_numeric's encoding looks inconsistent. Aggregates over channel and priority are well grounded.
